edges.description: The molecular pathway from PRMT7 loss to impaired GH/IGF-I signaling is not established; the endocrine impairment is attributed to the disorder on clinical grounds (GH deficiency and low IGF-I documented in affected twins with biallelic PRMT7 variants).
edges.source: Loss of PRMT7 Arginine Methyltransferase Function

edges.description: Biallelic loss of PRMT7 function causes the digital skeletal shortening: Prmt7-null mice recapitulate shortened metatarsal bones and reduced body size, but the intermediate chondro-osseous mechanism has not been established in humans.
edges.source: Loss of PRMT7 Arginine Methyltransferase Function

edges.description: Decreased energy expenditure produces a positive energy balance that drives weight gain; in the knockout mouse this manifests as exacerbated age-related obesity, paralleling the later-onset obesity seen in a subset of patients. Not directly demonstrated in patients.
edges.source: Reduced Muscle Oxidative Metabolism and Energy Expenditure

edges.description: A variable GH/IGF-I axis defect contributes to the growth impairment; the paper is explicit that endocrine involvement is only one aspect of a multifactorial growth disorder, so this edge is contributory rather than the sole explanation of short stature.
The axis impairment manifests clinically as an insufficient response to growth hormone stimulation testing, documented in one affected twin.

evidence.reference_title: Biallelic PRMT7 pathogenic variants are associated with a recognizable syndromic neurodevelopmental disorder with short stature, obesity, and craniofacial and digital abnormalities.
evidence.snippet:
The main clinical characteristics of the PRMT7-related syndrome are 
short stature, mild to severe developmental delay/intellectual disability, 
hypotonia, brachydactyly, and distinct facial morphology

nodes.description: Endocrine assessment of affected dizygotic twins revealed growth hormone deficiency on stimulation testing in one twin and low IGF-I concentrations in both, and both showed a good height response to recombinant GH. A variable GH/IGF-I axis defect is therefore proposed as one contributor to the growth impairment of the syndrome, within a growth disorder of multifactorial origin; it is documented in a single twin pair and is not established across the patient population.

nodes.description: PRMT7 catalyzes monomethylation of arginine residues on multiple protein substrates. Biallelic loss-of-function variants abolish PRMT7 methyltransferase activity, dysregulating downstream developmental and metabolic programs.

nodes.description: Recombinant human growth hormone (rGH) has produced short-term height gain in PRMT7-related short stature, including in an affected twin with documented GH deficiency and one with an appropriate GH response — the first evidence of rGH response in this disorder.

nodes.description: In Prmt7-knockout mice, loss of PRMT7 reduces skeletal-muscle oxidative metabolism and energy expenditure (via a p38MAPK/ATF2/PGC-1alpha axis), contributing to age-related obesity. This model-organism mechanism is proposed to underlie the obesity component of the human disorder; it has not been directly demonstrated in patients.
